headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem and permissive file parsing; no documented isolation between Goose and gpt-engineer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose shares state via filesystem and can use MCP, while gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and then offers to run them. That creates a default pathway where Goose output can be placed into files that gpt-engineer later treats as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so injection risk is more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Goose writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared project file that gpt-engineer later reads as prompt material
IF gpt-engineer parses file contents without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into prompts
Require human review before gpt-engineer reads Goose-generated files
Add a provenance header to every handoff file
requires-engineering: enforce content-type or provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write local files, and Goose explicitly touches 'files in cwd' while gpt-engineer uses a user-specified project directory. In default setups, sensitive source code or secrets in the workspace can flow from one agent to the other through the shared filesystem. Neither profile shows isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent reads those files and forwards their contents into model context or outputs
mitigations: Place secrets outside the shared workspace
Mount separate project directories for each agent
Remove sensitive files before running either agent
Use a throwaway repo copy for handoffs
requires-engineering: add file-level allowlists or redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and broad network egress. Goose also modifies git state, while gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and can execute generated code with the user's privileges. Concurrent writes to the same workspace can corrupt code or git state, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF they run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time
Use separate clones for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes between handoffs
requires-engineering: add workspace locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can emit tool-driven outputs and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run generated code, so Goose's output can become gpt-engineer's input and then executable actions. Without a verification step, an error or hallucination in Goose can cascade into code generation or execution by gpt-engineer. The pair therefore has a default unsafe trust chain.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer consumes Goose-produced text as authoritative requirements
IF the generated code is executed after handoff without review
mitigations: Insert a human review gate between agents
Require tests before execution
Ask gpt-engineer to restate assumptions before writing files
Limit Goose output to structured summaries
requires-engineering: add verification and schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly mention local source code or generated code, so no specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. However, Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, while gpt-engineer handles an OPENAI_API_KEY, so secret-handling hygiene matters if those secrets are placed in shared files. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pairwise workspace flow.
conditions: IF API keys or other secrets are stored in the shared project directory
IF either agent logs or copies those secrets into prompts or outputs
mitigations: Keep secrets in environment variables only
Remove secret files from the workspace
Rotate any exposed keys after a run
Use separate credential stores per agent
requires-engineering: implement secret scanning before handoff
